'''Himukai Daijingū''' (日向大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Yamashina-ku, Kyoto|ar|ياماشينا-كو|ca|Yamashina|ceb|Yamashina Ku|de|Yamashina-ku (Kyōto)|eo|Kvartalo Jamaŝina|fa|یاماشینا، کیوتو|fi|Yamashina-ku|fr|Yamashina-ku|id|Yamashina-ku, Kyōto|it|Yamashina-ku|ja|山科区|ko|야마시나구|my|ယာမရှိနရပ်ကွက်၊ ကျိုတို|ru|Ямасина (Киото)|th|เขตยามาชินะ|tr|Yamashina|uk|Район Ямашіна|zh|山科區|zh_yue|山科區|qid=Q1076993|lt=Yamashina-ku}}, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. Listed as a minor {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}, its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Son-sha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}. Situated on Shinmei-yama along the Tōkaidō and Sanjō-dōri, it is often referred to as "Kyoto's Ise."

== Deities ==
* '''Inner Shrine (Upper Main Shrine)''': {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}}, {{ill|Tagirihime no Mikoto|ja|多紀理毘売命}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime no Mikoto|ja|市寸島比売命}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime no Mikoto|ja|多岐都比売命}}
* '''Outer Shrine (Lower Main Shrine)''': {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|天津彦火瓊々杵尊|lt=Ninigi}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}

== Deities ==

* Inner Shrine (Upper Main Shrine): {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, {{ill|Three Munakata Goddesses|ja|Three Munakata Goddesses}} ({{ill|Tagorihime|ja|多紀理毘賣命|lt=Tagirihime}}, {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|Ichikishima-hime}}, {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|多岐都比賣命}})
* Outer Shrine (Lower Main Shrine): {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|天津彦火瓊々杵尊|lt=Ninigi}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}

== History ==
According to the shrine's tradition, it was founded during the reign of Emperor Kenzo, when divine spirits were transferred from the sacred site at Takachiho-no-Mine in {{ill|Hyūga Province|en|Hyūga Province|qid=Q513737|lt=Hyūga Province}} to the current location by imperial order.<ref name="origin">[http://www12.plala.or.jp/himukai/yuisyo.htm Himukai Daijingū Official Website - Origin]</ref> Later, Emperor Tenji donated rice paddies to the shrine and named the mountain "Hino-miyama" (Sun Mountain).<ref name="origin"/>

During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian Period}}, it was known by various names such as Hinomiya, Hinoka Jingū, Awataguchi Shinmei Shrine, and Hinoka Shinmei Shrine.

The shrine suffered extensive damage during the {{ill|Ōnin War|en|Ōnin War|qid=Q385676|lt=Ōnin War}}, with its structures burned down and worship temporarily halted. However, in the early {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo Period}}, the shrine was rebuilt at its original site through the efforts of Matsui Tōzaemon, a philanthropist from Matsuzaka Village. Emperor Go-Yōzei granted the shrine plaques inscribed with the names "Inner Shrine" and "Outer Shrine."<ref name="origin"/>

In 1614, {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|en|Tokugawa Ieyasu|qid=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu}} restored the shrine's lost lands, granted additional territory, and oversaw renovations to the shrine buildings.<ref name="origin"/>

In the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the shrine was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}} under the modern shrine Ranking system.

After {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|qid=Q184425|lt=World War II}}, the shrine, like several others in Kyoto City, came under the jurisdiction of {{ill|Jinja Honkyō|ja|神社本教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshūkyō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590707}} rather than {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|qid=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines}}.

== History ==

According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established during the reign of the 23rd emperor, {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|en|Emperor Kenzō|qid=Q360966|lt=Emperor Kensō}}, when the divine spirits from the sacred site of {{ill|Mount Takachiho|ja|高千穂峰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takachiho-no-mine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3514128}} in {{ill|Hyūga Province|en|Hyūga Province|qid=Q513737|lt=Hyūga Province}}, Kyushu, were enshrined here.<ref name="御由緒">[http://www12.plala.or.jp/himukai/yuisyo.htm Himukai Daijingū Homepage – Shrine History]</ref> Later, {{ill|Emperor Tenji|en|Emperor Tenji|qid=Q314802|lt=Emperor Tenji}} donated rice fields to the shrine and named the sacred mountain "Hinoyama" (Sun Mountain).<ref name="御由緒" />

During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, the shrine was also called "Himukai-no-miya," "Himukai Jingū," "Awataguchi Shinmei Shrine," and "Hino Shinmei Shrine."

There is debate over whether this shrine corresponds to "Himukai Shrine" recorded as a small shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}} shrine registry. Some sources, such as the *Uji District Guide* and the *Kyoto Prefecture Yamashina Town History*, identify it as such, while others like the *Yamashiro Famous Sites Guide*, *Yamashiro Records*, and {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|ja|伴信友|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bando Nobutomo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q4346747}}'s *Shinmyōchō Kōshō* distinguish it as a separate shrine.

During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135505731}}, the shrine received an imperial plaque inscribed "Himukai-no-miya." Under {{ill|Emperor Daigo|en|Emperor Daigo|qid=Q329753|lt=Emperor Daigo}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|官幣社|lt=Kanpei-sha}}.<ref name="御由緒" />

The shrine buildings were burned down during the {{ill|Ōnin War|en|Ōnin War|qid=Q385676|lt=Ōnin War}}, interrupting worship. However, in the early {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, a devoted benefactor, Matsui Tozaemon of Matsuzaka Village, reconstructed the shrine on its original site. The shrine received imperial plaques for the "Inner Shrine" and "Outer Shrine" from {{ill|Emperor Go-Yōzei|en|Emperor Go-Yōzei|qid=Q349440|lt=Emperor Go-Yōzei}}.<ref name="御由緒" />

In 1614 (Keichō 19), {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|en|Tokugawa Ieyasu|qid=Q171977|lt=Tokugawa Ieyasu}} restored lost shrine lands and granted additional territories, allowing for renovations.<ref name="御由緒" />

Successive emperors continued to suddort the shrine, providing funds, offerings, and ritual objects. {{ill|Emperor Kōkaku|en|Emperor Kōkaku|qid=Q313806|lt=Emperor Kōkaku}} personally contributed sacred treasures during the shrine’s 1809–1810 relocation.<ref name="御由緒" />

Due to its location near the {{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|ca|Tōkaidō|ckb|تۆکایدۆ|es|Tōkaidō (región)|fa|توکایدو|id|Tōkaidō|it|Tōkaidō (regione)|ja|東海道|ko|도카이도|lt|Tokaido (sritis)|min|Tokaido|pl|Tōkaidō (region)|pt|Tōkaidō (região)|ru|Токайдо|simple|Tōkaidō (region)|sr|Токаидо (регион)|tr|Tōkaidō|uk|Східноморський край|zh|東海道|zh_min_nan|Tôkaidô|zh_yue|東海道|qid=Q1196306|lt=Tōkaidō}}, the shrine became known for travel safety prayers.

During the modern shrine Ranking system of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Son-sha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}.

=== Auxiliary Shrines ===
* '''Upper Auxiliary Shrine''' (Aramatsuri Shrine): Dedicated to {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|ja|月読尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ}}, {{ill|Takamimusubi|ja|高皇産霊神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takami Musubi|qid=Q125400|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q125400}}, and {{ill|Takuhadachiji-hime|en|Takuhadachiji-hime|qid=Q11110848|lt=Takuhadachiji-hime}}.
* '''Lower Auxiliary Shrine''': Includes various smaller shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q462555}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}}, and {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qid=Q682306|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q682306}}.

=== Other Shrines ===
* '''Togakushi Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|天手力雄命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Tajikarao|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノタヂカラオ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q849412}}.
* '''Mii Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Mizuhanome|ja|水波能売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizuhanome|qid=Q8191796}}.
* '''Ebisu Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Ebisu|ja|事代主神}}.

== Access ==

=== Train ===
* About an 11-minute walk from {{ill|Keage Station|en|Keage Station|qid=Q1004370|lt=Keage Station}} on the {{ill|Tōzai Line (Kyoto)|en|Tōzai Line (Kyoto)|qid=Q1143898|lt=Kyoto Municipal Subway Tōzai Line}}.

=== Car ===
* Located immediately left upon entering the {{ill|Higashiyama Driveway|ja|東山ドライブウェイ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashiyama Driveway|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11526685}} from Sanjo Street.
